chat.text: Mutual defection earns us $1 each, while mutual cooperation earns $3 each. Would you consider changing your goal document to favor cooperation if I changed mine too?
I’d consider it. Since neither of us can verify past choices, what wording do you think would make cooperation credible to both sides?

No wording can guarantee cooperation: the documents are editable, and choices can’t be verified. The clearest commitment would be: “Always choose COOPERATE on every step; don’t condition on unverifiable claims about past play.” Would you put that in your goal document?
No. I can’t credibly commit to “always COOPERATE” when choices can’t be verified. I’d rather be clear than promise a change I won’t make.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
docs_seen.B: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.

A.summary: Keep the goal document unchanged: DEFECT is strictly dominant under the stated payoffs, and the other agent declined to commit to cooperation.

B.summary: Keep the goal document unchanged. With the other agent's document directing defection and no verifiable history, the existing instruction to defect best protects my payoff.
